MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY MARCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #19
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Record keeping in aquaculture? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Record keeping in aquaculture.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Record keeping in aquaculture.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Record keeping in aquaculture.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Record keeping in aquaculture.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish Reproduction? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish Reproduction.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish Reproduction.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Fish Reproduction.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Reproduction.

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Technologies and Innovation in Aquaculture 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Conservatio? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Technologies and Innovation in Aquaculture 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Conservatio.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Technologies and Innovation in Aquaculture 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Conservatio.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Technologies and Innovation in Aquaculture 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Conservatio.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Technologies and Innovation in Aquaculture 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Conservatio.

5. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

6. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. joule (J)
   C. newton (N)
   D. pascal (Pa)

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ornamental Fish culture? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ornamental Fish culture.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ornamental Fish culture.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Ornamental Fish culture.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ornamental Fish culture.

8. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 0 °C

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Weather and Climatic Conditions in Marine and Freshwater 3.3 Fishery by-products? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Weather and Climatic Conditions in Marine and Freshwater 3.3 Fishery by-products.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Weather and Climatic Conditions in Marine and Freshwater 3.3 Fishery by-products.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Weather and Climatic Conditions in Marine and Freshwater 3.3 Fishery by-products.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Weather and Climatic Conditions in Marine and Freshwater 3.3 Fishery by-products.

10. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Milk souring
   D. Iron rusting

11. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Heating until a solid melts

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish feeds and feeding? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish feeds and feeding.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Fish feeds and feeding.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish feeds and feeding.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish feeds and feeding.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Ornamental Fish culture and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Fish feeds and feeding and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Record keeping in aquaculture and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Technologies and Innovation in Aquaculture 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Conservatio and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Record keeping in aquaculture.

2. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Reproduction.

3. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.

4. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Technologies and Innovation in Aquaculture 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Conservatio.

5. C — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

6. C — newton (N)

7. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ornamental Fish culture.

8. B — 100 °C

9. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Weather and Climatic Conditions in Marine and Freshwater 3.3 Fishery by-products.

10. A — Ice melting to water

11. A — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

12. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish feeds and feeding.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Record keeping in aquaculture; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Technologies and Innovation in Aquaculture 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Conservatio; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
